inspiration.observed_pattern: A recursive CTE expands each input string into one row per character, carries the preceding character, conditionally changes letter case at token boundaries, and reassembles each string with ordered GROUP_CONCAT.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored title-normalization report. A recursive positions CTE scans fixed snippet text, a character CTE exposes the preceding character, CASE uses REGEXP plus UPPER/LOWER at punctuation boundaries, and ordered GROUP_CONCAT rebuilds each normalized title. The source schema, values, aliases, and application purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Snippet 101 starts with letters and contains a hyphen plus digits before a new word; snippet 102 starts with digits and uses punctuation before its next word. Each alphabetic token's first character is uppercased and later letters are lowercased, while digits and punctuation remain unchanged.
determinism_notes: Snippet IDs, source text, recursive positions, character ordering, and final ordering are fixed; there are no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE title_snippets (snippet_id INT PRIMARY KEY, raw_text VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO title_snippets VALUES (101, 'alpha BETA-42 gamma'), (102, '9lEVEL!NEXT phase')

steps.sql: WITH RECURSIVE positions AS (SELECT snippet_id, raw_text, 1 AS pos, CHAR_LENGTH(raw_text) AS text_len FROM title_snippets UNION ALL SELECT snippet_id, raw_text, pos + 1, text_len FROM positions WHERE pos < text_len), chars AS (SELECT snippet_id, raw_text, pos, SUBSTRING(raw_text, pos, 1) AS ch, CASE WHEN pos = 1 THEN NULL ELSE SUBSTRING(raw_text, pos - 1, 1) END AS prev_ch FROM positions) SELECT snippet_id, raw_text, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN pos = 1 OR (prev_ch NOT REGEXP '[A-Za-z]' AND ch REGEXP '[A-Za-z]') THEN UPPER(ch) ELSE LOWER(ch) END ORDER BY pos SEPARATOR '') AS normalized_text FROM chars GROUP BY snippet_id, raw_text ORDER BY snippet_id
